open_points.subject: Effectful operation send preconditions vs owner-approval stop rule
open_points.text: K-08: "At run time each `state-transition`, `external-effect` and `destructive` node stops for the owner's approval ..."; A11 rule 1: "Reaching an operation element runs in this order: the pre-send checks of A09 rule 6 ... then the authority of A10 rule 1".
open_points.question: If an effectful node fails a pre-send check (for example `binding_stale` or missing instance), must it still stop and create an approval request first, or fail immediately without any approval record?
options: Pre-send checks run first and may fail the element without requesting approval.
Approval is always requested first for these classes, even if a pre-send check would fail.
open_points.default_guess: Pre-send checks first, fail immediately without approval (follow A11 ordering).

open_points.subject: Function filesystem purity boundary
open_points.text: K-02: function has "no filesystem beyond its input"; A03 rule 1: sandbox provides "one private exchange directory" and audit allows opening paths inside it.
open_points.question: Are function implementations allowed to read/write arbitrary files inside the exchange directory, or should filesystem access be limited strictly to declared file-port inputs/outputs only?
options: Allow filesystem IO inside the private exchange directory.
Disallow general filesystem IO and permit only declared file-port payload handling paths.
open_points.default_guess: Allow IO inside the private exchange directory (follow A03).

open_points.subject: Cycle detection semantics with guards
open_points.text: A05 phase 7: "cycles: the graph of nodes and edges is acyclic;" (no guard-specific qualification).
open_points.question: When checking acyclicity, are guarded edges always included as graph edges, or only edges that can deliver under some guard valuation considered?
options: Include all declared edges regardless of guards.
Exclude or conditionally include guarded edges based on deliverability.

open_points.subject: Repeated path placeholders in operation path
open_points.text: A09 rule 2: "every `{name}` in the path takes the input port of that name ... An input placed in the path is placed nowhere else".
open_points.question: If the same placeholder name appears multiple times in the path, is that valid (same input substituted in each occurrence), or should such a binding be refused as ambiguous?
options: Allow repeats and substitute the same input value at each occurrence.
Refuse paths with repeated placeholder names.

open_points.subject: WaitingPoint replacement semantics across reason changes
open_points.text: A14 rule 1 defines waiting points by reason; A11 rule 3 says resolving `not_applied` makes the element "waits again with reason `owner_approval`".
open_points.question: For one element transitioning from `outcome_unknown` to `owner_approval`, does the kernel replace the existing waiting point or keep multiple waiting points for that element over time?
options: Maintain at most one current waiting point per element and replace reason on transition.
Append a new waiting point entry and keep prior waiting entries concurrently.
open_points.default_guess: Replace with one current waiting point per element.
